Most of it could be summarized with the old concept of "God of the gaps" - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_the_gaps - where people try to point gaps in knowledge as evidence of supreme beings... when in fact they just prove that there's a lot we don't know yet.

The panspermia hypothesis always fascinated me, and I don't even find it unreasonable in principle, but at this point it isn't even a proper theory, just genuine speculation without much hard evidence to back it. Beside that, even its confirmation wouldn't really prove the existence of a God, just that life's origin is a lot more complex and surprising than we used to think.

About the weirdest scenarios like the holographic universe or the "computer simulation universe" (note: they are eventually compatible and could even end reinforcing each other, but not strictly part of the same theory) I've read about them in the past and I have to admit I feel like I never really grasped on what they are building upon. Until we'll know more I'd be incline to dismiss them as "smart people entertaining themselves with a mathematical model and trying to put it to test".

Oh, and just to offer a full disclosure: I'm an atheist myself, so yeah, I have my bias in that sense.
